rules.description: Tool input and output schemas must be valid under their applicable JSON Schema dialect. Unsupported declared dialects are errors; unresolved external references warn when complete offline checking is unavailable. External schemas are not fetched automatically, and a partial check is not reported as complete.
rules.notes: The declared dialect set is fixed by the specification, not by the validator: an unsupported dialect is an error, not a warning, because MCP guarantees only 2020-12 support and peers return an error for other dialects, and because Tool examples cannot be checked against a schema in an unknown dialect (maintainer decision on issue #72, 2026-10-26). Unresolved external references differ: offline validation forbids retrieving them, so they only warn. Earlier protocol versions define no embedded dialect; mcp.tool.schema.legacy-shape applies to those protocol versions instead.

arbitrations.behavior: Reject a declared root type that excludes "object"; accept other roots that are valid under the dialect, which mcp.tool.schema.native-shape reports as warnings.
arbitrations.conflict: The specification validates the outputSchema under its declared or default dialect, while schema.ts requires the JSON Schema keyword and value type "object" at the root. A root in allOf or $ref can describe an object without matching the TypeScript type.
arbitrations.rationale: One position for every conflict between MCP's dialect text and the schema syntax of its TypeScript types (Proposal 0032): MCP Description enforces what MCP requires of the data and reports, but does not decide, the narrower TypeScript syntax.
arbitrations.reviewTrigger: Resolution of MCP issue 3238 or an MCP erratum for 2025-11-25.

rules.description: MCP 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 require structured output to be an object. For MCP 2025-06-18 the outputSchema root declares type object. For MCP 2025-11-25 a declared root type must include object; a root without a literal type object stays valid and mcp.tool.schema.native-shape warns. MCP 2026-07-28 permits other roots, so an array schema needs a scope that excludes the object-only versions; projection must not wrap it in an object as a repair.

gaps.behavior: The object-root check also runs where outputSchema is not defined, so a non-object outputSchema reports this error in addition to the protocol-version applicability error.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 schema.ts, interface Tool, outputSchema (type "object")
MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface Tool, outputSchema (no root type)
MCP 2025-11-25 specification, Basic, JSON Schema usage (schemas are validated under their declared or default dialect)

rules.summary: Before MCP 2026-07-28, a Tool outputSchema describes an object: a literal type "object" for MCP 2025-06-18, and a declared root type that includes "object" for MCP 2025-11-25.
rules.title: Use object output schemas before MCP 2026

rules.description: Tool outputSchema is available from MCP 2025-06-18. A Tool whose effective scope includes an earlier protocol version cannot carry it unchanged. Omit it for the earlier version or provide disjoint variants.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-03-26 schema.ts, interface Tool (closed; no outputSchema)
MCP 2025-06-18 schema.ts, interface Tool, outputSchema

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 9.1 (Tool Object field table)

rules.summary: A Tool declares outputSchema only for MCP protocol versions whose Tool type defines it.
rules.title: Declare output schemas only where MCP defines them

arbitrations.authority: MCP schema.ts doc comment, consistent with MCP 2026-07-28
arbitrations.behavior: Accept and preserve any JSON Schema keyword in these protocol versions.
arbitrations.conflict: The TypeScript type of inputSchema (and outputSchema from 2025-06-18) lists only type, properties, required, and from 2025-11-25 $schema, with no index signature, while its doc comment defines the value as a JSON Schema object.
arbitrations.rationale: A JSON Schema object admits any keyword. MCP 2026-07-28 makes this explicit with an index signature, and rejecting keywords such as $defs or $ref would reject Tools that MCP clients accept.
arbitrations.reviewTrigger: An upstream clarification or erratum for the earlier protocol versions.

rules.description: Embedded Tool schemas can contain keywords beyond the fields MCP lists. A tool must preserve them through the operations covered by the specification instead of discarding unrecognized keywords. This is a tooling guarantee, so a valid custom keyword does not itself produce a document diagnostic.

sources.reference: MCP 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25 schema.ts, interface Tool, inputSchema and outputSchema doc comments ("A JSON Schema object")
MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface Tool, inputSchema and outputSchema (index signature [key: string]: unknown)

rules.summary: Tool inputSchema and outputSchema are JSON Schema objects; keywords beyond those MCP lists are permitted and preserved, and acquire MCP semantics only where a protocol version defines them.
rules.title: Retain embedded JSON Schema keywords

rules.description: Early MCP protocol versions define a limited Tool-schema shape without a default embedded dialect. Check the known properties and required-name list without rejecting other keywords using an inferred meta-schema. Incomplete example validation is reported separately.
rules.notes: From MCP 2025-11-25 the embedded dialect governs these keywords (json-schema.tool-schema.valid); mcp.tool.schema.native-shape warns where the MCP 2025-11-25 Tool type is narrower.

sources.reference: MCP 2024-11-05 to 2025-06-18 schema.ts, interface Tool, inputSchema (and outputSchema from 2025-06-18): properties?: { [key: string]: object }, required?: string[]

rules.summary: Before MCP 2025-11-25, Tool schema properties is an object of objects and required is an array of strings; other keywords are preserved.
rules.title: Check early Tool schemas without inferring a dialect

arbitrations.authority: MCP specification text on schema dialects
arbitrations.behavior: Accept the schema, report a warning naming the protocol versions concerned, and let native projection fail its postcondition for them.
arbitrations.conflict: MCP validates embedded schemas under their declared or default dialect, JSON Schema 2020-12 by default, which allows boolean subschemas and roots in $ref or allOf. The TypeScript Tool type requires a literal type "object" at the inputSchema root, and in MCP 2025-11-25 also at the outputSchema root and an object for each top-level properties value.
arbitrations.rationale: The conflict is internal to MCP, so MCP Description reports it instead of deciding it (Proposal 0032). MCP 2026-07-28 removed the properties restriction, the official SDKs accept boolean property subschemas, and authors can always meet the restriction without changing the meaning of the schema.
arbitrations.reviewTrigger: Resolution of MCP issue 3238 or an MCP erratum for 2025-11-25.

rules.description: From MCP 2025-11-25, an embedded Tool schema is judged by its JSON Schema dialect, but the MCP Tool type still restricts some schema syntax: a literal type object at the inputSchema root, and for MCP 2025-11-25 at the outputSchema root and an object for each top-level properties value. A schema that misses a restriction stays valid and receives a warning naming the protocol versions concerned, because its native projection for them fails. Use {} instead of true, {"not": {}} instead of false, add type object beside $ref or allOf, or narrow the Tool's protocolVersions.
rules.notes: Only a declared root type is examined; composition is not analyzed to prove that a root admits objects. Nested schemas and keywords other than top-level properties are not restricted by any MCP Tool type.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-11-25 schema.ts, interface Tool: inputSchema and outputSchema have type: "object" and properties?: { [key: string]: object }
MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface Tool: inputSchema has type: "object" and an open index signature; outputSchema has no root type
MCP 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 specification, Basic, JSON Schema usage (schemas are validated under their declared or default dialect)
Official TypeScript SDK, Tool schema: any JSON value under properties, type: z.literal('object') at the inputSchema root

rules.summary: A Tool schema that is valid under its dialect but misses a schema-syntax restriction of the MCP Tool type for an applicable protocol version is accepted with a warning.
rules.title: Report Tool schemas that MCP Tool types reject

rules.description: A successful Tool example for a Tool with outputSchema must carry the required structuredContent. The schema describes that structured value, not the unstructured content array. Check success and error examples separately before deciding which payload is missing.
rules.notes: Conformance of structuredContent to outputSchema is checked by mcpdesc.tool.example.schema-conformance. Error results are governed by mcpdesc.tool.example.error-result.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 specification, Server Features, Tools, Output Schema ("Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema")

rules.summary: When a Tool declares outputSchema, a successful result contains structuredContent.
rules.title: Supply structured content when an output schema needs it

rules.description: Legacy HTTP plus SSE remains representable but is deprecated for later MCP protocol versions. The warning does not by itself invalidate the document. Review whether the server still offers that transport or whether the description should advertise Streamable HTTP instead.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-03-26 specification, Basic, Transports, Backwards Compatibility (deprecated HTTP+SSE transport)

rules.summary: Legacy HTTP+SSE associated with MCP 2025-03-26 or later is reported, because Streamable HTTP replaces it.
rules.title: Review deprecated legacy SSE transports

rules.description: Streamable HTTP is not defined by the earliest supported MCP protocol version. Scope the transport to versions that define it and keep root protocol coverage consistent. A URL alone does not make a transport applicable to every protocol version.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-03-26 specification, Basic, Transports, Streamable HTTP (replaces HTTP+SSE from 2024-11-05)

rules.summary: Streamable HTTP is used only from MCP 2025-03-26.
rules.title: Use Streamable HTTP only where supported

rules.description: A completion example must target a Prompt argument or Resource Template variable that exists. Context entries must name other declared targets, not repeat the argument being completed. Correct the example names or the declaration they describe.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, CompleteRequest context.arguments (previously-resolved variables in a URI template or prompt)

rules.summary: A completion example completes a declared Prompt argument or URI template variable, and its context names other declared arguments or variables only.
rules.title: Complete a declared argument or template variable

rules.description: The components object holds non-empty named maps in its five namespaces. A Reference Object has exactly one $componentRef. Where a value may be inline or a reference, the inline form is a JSON object without $componentRef.
rules.summary: Components contain non-empty, well-named maps; a Reference Object has only $componentRef; an inline schema or example is an object.
rules.title: Shape components and Reference Objects

rules.description: A component reference must identify an existing value in the namespace required by its use site, without a reference cycle. Check both the target name and the namespace. Reuse does not exempt the resolved value from validation in its containing declaration.
rules.summary: A Reference Object targets an existing component in the namespace its use site requires, without cycles.
rules.title: Resolve component references in the right namespace

rules.description: The document root has the required mcpdesc, info, and protocolVersions members, only the members of Section 3.2, and non-empty ordinary collections. Failures inside a root member belong to the rule that owns that member's schema location; this rule reports root-level failures.
rules.notes: The optional root $schema does not select the schema used for validation: optional-schema-omitted.json omits it and validates against the schema for its mcpdesc version.
rules.summary: A document validates against the JSON Schema for its declared mcpdesc version. This rule owns the document root and generic JSON values; every other schema location belongs to a more specific rule.
rules.title: Match the MCP Description document schema

rules.description: Form properties, required names, enum labels, defaults, and bounds must agree with one another. Correct references to absent properties and contradictory constraints. Passing JSON Schema's outer shape checks does not prove that the declared form is internally consistent.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, PrimitiveSchemaDefinition and EnumSchema (enumNames are display names for enum values)

rules.summary: A form requestedSchema is internally consistent: required names declared properties, enumNames match enum values, defaults lie within enums, and minimum bounds do not exceed maximum bounds.
rules.title: Keep elicitation form constraints consistent

rules.description: An elicitation declaration has a name, a mode, and a message. Form mode requires requestedSchema and forbids url; URL mode requires url and forbids requestedSchema. Unknown properties are rejected.
rules.summary: An Elicitation Declaration has its required fields, the fields of its mode only, and no unknown properties.
rules.title: Declare elicitations with their mode fields

rules.description: Elicitation declaration names identify interactions within their primitive. Duplicate names make a Tool interaction's declaration reference ambiguous. Rename one declaration and update the references that are intended to select it.
rules.summary: Elicitation Declaration names are unique within their primitive.
rules.title: Give each elicitation declaration a unique name

rules.description: An example result is the completed payload, not a JSON-RPC response or a pending workflow. Remove envelope fields such as jsonrpc and id and do not include task or input-required state. Multi-step interactions belong in the explicit interaction example structure.
rules.notes: Envelope fields are jsonrpc, id, and error. Non-completed workflow fields are task, inputRequests, and requestState. They are excluded from the field classification of mcp.result.additional-properties.preserve.

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, InputRequiredResult (inputRequests, requestState) and Result.resultType
MCP 2025-11-25 schema.ts, CreateTaskResult (task)

rules.summary: An example result is a completed result payload: it contains no JSON-RPC envelope field and no non-completed workflow field.
rules.title: Show completed results without message envelopes

rules.description: Named example maps are non-empty, use names matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, and hold an example object or a Reference Object. Each example object has its required members, such as input and result, and only its defined properties.
rules.summary: Example maps and Tool, Resource, Resource Template, Prompt, and completion example objects have valid names, required members, and no unknown properties.
rules.surface: Tool, Resource, Resource Template, Prompt, and completion examples
rules.title: Shape named example maps and example objects

rules.description: A completed example result must contain the fields each applicable MCP protocol version requires, with valid values. Check the result's full effective scope, not only the newest version. Fields permitted but undefined on open result types are handled separately as warnings.
rules.notes: Fields an MCP protocol version does not define are governed by mcp.result.additional-properties.preserve (accepted with a warning). When present, resultType must be "complete", ttlMs non-negative, and cacheScope "public" or "private" in every applicable protocol version (document schema).

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface Result (resultType required) and interface CacheableResult (ttlMs, cacheScope required)

specification.reference: Examples fail fast decision (validation README, 2026-10-25, issue #72)

rules.summary: An example result contains every field that each applicable MCP protocol version requires, and every field a protocol version defines has a valid value.
rules.title: Match example results to every applicable version

rules.description: Extension identifiers in an MCP-reserved namespace are checked against the pinned catalogue. Unknown or experimental identifiers are preserved with a warning. Verify the identifier and its maturity; an unrecognized identifier is not silently assigned known extension semantics.
rules.notes: The pinned catalogue lists no experimental identifiers, so no document currently produces the experimental-identifier warning.

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 specification, Basic, General fields, _meta key name format (second label modelcontextprotocol or mcp is reserved)

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Sections 8.4 and 8.5; validator extension catalogue (effective 2026-09-04)

rules.summary: An extension identifier under an MCP-reserved prefix that the pinned extension catalogue lists as experimental, or does not list, is preserved with a warning.
rules.title: Review reserved extension identifiers

rules.description: The required info object names and versions the server. Its contact and license objects are closed and follow the property tables of Section 5.
rules.summary: Info has a non-empty name and version, and Info, Contact, and License contain only their defined properties with the defined types.
rules.title: Describe the server in a valid Info Object

rules.description: MCP 2024-11-05 and 2025-03-26 receive structural and selected checks, not a claim of complete MCP semantic conformance. The warning describes a validation limitation rather than an invalid document. Adding a later protocol version does not make checks for the earlier versions complete.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Sections 3.5 and 16.2; Proposal 0024, Section 4.1

rules.summary: A document applying to MCP 2024-11-05 or 2025-03-26 is reported as receiving structural and selected checks only, not complete MCP semantic conformance.
rules.title: Limited validation for early MCP protocol versions

rules.description: Native projection selects a Tool, Resource, Resource Template, or Prompt by its identifier in one protocol view. A declaration outside that view cannot be projected for that version. Check the identifier and the declaration's inherited or explicit scope.
rules.notes: Implemented by @mcpdesc/core; this repository checks the fixtures with scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs.
rules.summary: Native projection selects one declaration of the requested kind and identifier in the Effective Protocol View for the protocol version.
rules.title: Select an applicable declaration for projection

rules.description: Native projection resolves Tool schema components, removes description-only fields, and checks the value against the selected MCP schema. It does not repair values or invent defaults. A postcondition failure returns no projected value. It is an implementation or specification defect, unless validation warned about the Tool schema under mcp.tool.schema.native-shape for that protocol version.
rules.notes: The postcondition cases come from Tool schemas that are valid under their JSON Schema dialect but miss a schema-syntax restriction of the MCP Tool type (Proposal 0032), not from an injected fault: the source is valid with a warning, yet the native value fails the pinned MCP schema. A list fails as a whole. scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs checks that each failure case's value really fails that schema and that every expected value passes it.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 4.14, steps 4 to 6, no synthesis, and lists

rules.summary: A native projection keeps exactly the declaration fields that the MCP type defines in the protocol version, unchanged after reference resolution, and the value validates against the pinned MCP schema for that protocol version.
rules.title: Preserve MCP values when projecting declarations

rules.description: Native projection first validates the source and checks that the requested MCP protocol version appears at the root. Fix source errors or select a declared version. These failures come from the projection operation, not a new document-validation phase.
rules.notes: Implemented by @mcpdesc/core; this repository checks the fixtures with scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs.
rules.summary: Native projection starts from a document without validation errors and from a protocol version in its root protocolVersions.
rules.title: Project a valid source and declared protocol version

rules.description: A Prompt example supplies every required argument and no undeclared argument. Check names against the containing Prompt, including when the example comes from a reusable component. Omitted optional arguments do not need placeholder values.

sources.reference: MCP 2024-11-05 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface PromptArgument, required ("Whether this argument must be provided")

rules.summary: A Prompt example supplies every required Prompt argument and no undeclared argument.
rules.title: Supply the Prompt arguments the example requires

rules.description: A Prompt has a name, and each argument has a name. Both accept only the properties of their Section 11 tables, each with its defined type.
rules.summary: Prompt and Prompt Argument Objects have their required fields, defined property types, and no unknown properties.
rules.title: Declare Prompts and arguments with their fields

rules.description: An omitted scope inherits its parent's full scope; an explicit child scope must stay within it. Declarations with the same identity cannot overlap where the specification requires uniqueness. Narrow the scopes rather than expecting the validator to choose one variant.
rules.summary: Nested protocol scopes stay within their parent scope, and same-named primitives and capability objects do not overlap in protocol scope.
rules.title: Keep protocol scopes consistent and disjoint

rules.description: Root and declaration protocolVersions arrays are non-empty, contain no duplicates, and name only MCP protocol versions this specification supports.
rules.summary: A protocolVersions array is non-empty, has unique values, and contains only supported MCP protocol-version identifiers.
rules.title: List supported MCP protocol versions in protocol scopes

rules.description: A Resource Template example records the concrete requested URI, which must be an RFC 6570 expansion of the containing template. Check the template and URI together, including examples reached through components. Matching a URI does not require network retrieval.

sources.reference: RFC 6570, URI Template

rules.summary: A Resource Template example uri is a valid RFC 6570 expansion of the template.
rules.title: Use a concrete URI that expands the template

rules.description: Resource example contents are compared with the declaration's requested URI, MIME type, and declared raw size. A mutable resource can differ between observations, so size differences are warnings. Review the example and declaration together rather than inferring live content.
rules.notes: Collections and indirect reads may legitimately differ, so these are warnings.
rules.summary: Resource example contents agree with their declaration: the requested URI is returned, MIME types match, and raw size matches a declared size.
rules.title: Keep Resource examples consistent with declarations

rules.description: A Resource has a uri and a name; a Resource Template has a uriTemplate and a name. Both accept only the properties of their Section 10 tables, each with its defined type.
rules.summary: Resource and Resource Template Objects have their required fields, defined property types, and no unknown properties.
rules.title: Declare Resources and templates with their fields

rules.description: Named security schemes are non-empty and each scheme has a type and the fields that type requires, such as OAuth flows with their URLs and scopes. Unknown properties are rejected.
rules.summary: securitySchemes is a non-empty map of Security Scheme Objects that contain their type-specific required fields and only defined properties.
rules.title: Define security schemes with their required fields

rules.description: Security requirements refer to named schemes, and scopes have meaning only for OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect schemes. Correct missing references or repeated scopes. An uncatalogued scope can produce a warning where the scheme declares a static scope catalogue.
rules.notes: The document schema rejects duplicate scopes first; the semantic duplicate-scope check applies only to direct callers of the semantic validator.
rules.summary: Security requirements name declared schemes, list scopes only for OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect schemes, do not repeat scopes, and use catalogued scopes when the scheme declares a static catalogue.
rules.title: Reference security schemes and scopes correctly

rules.description: A document is UTF-8 JSON or a single restricted YAML document that decodes to the JSON data model: string keys only, no duplicate keys, tags, or aliases, no merge semantics, and only finite numbers. Rejected YAML is not validated further.
rules.notes: Checked when a serialization is decoded, before document validation, so a validator that receives decoded data reports this rule as delegated. Checked by decoding the serialization fixtures; scripts/test-serializations.mjs also checks that the equivalent JSON and YAML documents decode and validate identically.
rules.summary: A document uses a conforming serialization: RFC 8259 JSON in UTF-8, or exactly one YAML document within the restricted YAML profile.
rules.title: Serialize documents as JSON or restricted YAML

rules.description: Each entry of the root tags catalogue is a Tag Object with a name and only the properties of Section 13.1.
rules.summary: A Tag Object has a non-empty name and only its defined properties.
rules.title: Declare tags with a name

rules.description: When the document declares a tag catalogue, primitive tag references must name entries in it. Root tag names and repeated primitive references are checked for duplicates. Fix the name or catalogue entry instead of relying on an undeclared alias.
rules.summary: Root tag names are unique, and primitives reference only declared tags.
rules.title: Reference unique declared tags

rules.description: Tool execution errors are completed MCP Tool results with isError true, not a separate description-only error catalogue. Check the error result's content and avoid presenting successful structured output as the error payload.
rules.notes: MCP does not forbid structuredContent on error results; MCP Description requires its absence so that example structuredContent always conforms to outputSchema.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 9.3 (an execution-error result MUST NOT contain structuredContent; outputSchema does not validate error content)

rules.summary: A Tool execution-error example result sets isError to true and does not contain structuredContent.
rules.title: Represent Tool execution errors as error results

rules.description: Example input must satisfy the resolved inputSchema, and successful structured output must satisfy outputSchema when supplied. Correct the example or the declaration's schema. Where resolution or dialect support prevents complete checking, the diagnostic must make that limitation visible.
rules.notes: Before MCP 2025-11-25 no embedded dialect is defined, so only the legacy shape is checked and the warning reports the gap.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 specification, Server Features, Tools, Output Schema (structured results conform to outputSchema)

rules.summary: A Tool example input validates against inputSchema, and its structuredContent against outputSchema, for every applicable protocol version; incomplete validation is reported.
rules.title: Check Tool examples against their schemas

rules.description: A Tool interaction example can contradict its explicit minimum client requirements. Review the warning against the scenario and the declared requirements. The example does not automatically create or strengthen a client requirement.
rules.notes: Steps never create requirements; the warning reports a contradiction only.
rules.summary: Interaction steps do not contradict the Tool's explicit client capability requirements.
rules.title: Keep interactions consistent with client requirements

rules.description: A Tool's elicitation step must agree with the named elicitation declaration and its requested form. Accepted form content must satisfy that schema, while declined or cancelled responses have different content rules. Check the reference, request, and response together.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface ElicitResult, content (present for accepted form responses)

rules.summary: An elicitation step matches the Tool's named Elicitation Declaration, and its response content is present exactly when an accepted form response requires it and validates against the requested schema.
rules.title: Match elicitation steps to their declaration

rules.description: A Tool interaction example has input, ordered steps, and a result. Each step is an elicitation, sampling, or roots step with its request and response, and accepts only its defined properties.
rules.summary: Interaction examples and steps have their required members, a known step type, and no unknown properties.
rules.title: Shape Tool interaction examples and steps

rules.description: A Tool has a non-empty name and an inputSchema, and accepts only the properties of the Section 9.1 table, each with its defined type. The execution object accepts only taskSupport.
rules.summary: A Tool Object has its required fields, defined property types, and no unknown properties; so does its Execution Object.
rules.title: Declare Tools with their defined fields

rules.description: A transport is Streamable HTTP, stdio, or legacy SSE, selected by type. Each type requires its own fields, such as url or command, and accepts only the properties in its Section 6.2 table.
rules.summary: A Transport Object matches exactly one transport type and contains its required fields and only its defined properties.
rules.title: Declare transports with their type-specific fields

rules.description: When transports are declared, every root protocol version must be covered by at least one transport's effective scope. An omitted transport scope inherits all root versions. Add appropriate coverage or narrow the documented protocol versions rather than leaving an unreachable view. Descriptions may omit transports entirely.
rules.summary: Every protocol version at the root is covered by at least one transport when transports are declared.
rules.title: Cover each declared protocol version with a transport

rules.description: A merge validates every input, requires equivalent views for a shared protocol version and equal unscoped metadata, collapses equivalent declarations, keeps differing ones as disjoint variants, renames colliding components, and fails rather than guess when inputs conflict.
rules.notes: Checked by the cases in view-fixtures/; scripts/test-view-fixtures.mjs also checks the round-trip invariant of Section 4.13 for every merge result.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 4.13, and the merge requirements of Sections 13, 14, and 17

rules.summary: A merge result is valid, preserves every input protocol-version view, and fails on any conflict it cannot represent faithfully.
rules.title: Merge protocol views without guessing

rules.description: A single-version projection validates the source, keeps the declarations whose effective scope includes the protocol version, removes their scopes, and keeps everything else unchanged: security forms, examples, client requirements, tags, extensions, and the components still referenced.
rules.notes: Checked by the cases in view-fixtures/, which scripts/test-view-fixtures.mjs recomputes with the reference operations of scripts/mcpdesc-views.mjs. Implementations such as @mcpdesc/core must pass them.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 4.12, and the view requirements of Sections 3 to 17

rules.summary: An Effective Protocol View is a valid document for one protocol version that keeps the applicable declarations and preserves their content, security semantics, and referenced components.
rules.title: Project a document to one MCP protocol version
